design.system:
P = 4-(4-bromobutyl)benzonitrile
P --[(i) DIBAL-H; (ii) H₂O]--> Q
Q --[CH₃OH (excess), dry HCl]--> R
R --[(i) potassium phthalimide; (ii) NaOH (aq), heat]--> S
R --[dry Ag₂O, heat]--> T
R --[alc. KOH, heat]--> U
design.hidden_link: DIBAL-H reduces the nitrile to an aldehyde (Q). Acetal formation protects the aldehyde to give R. Gabriel phthalimide synthesis on the primary bromide yields exclusively a primary amine (S). Treatment with dry Ag₂O forms a symmetrical ether (T) rather than an alcohol.
design.route:
1. P to Q: DIBAL-H stops at the imine, which hydrolyzes to an aldehyde. Q has an aldehyde and an alkyl bromide.
2. Q to R: Methanol and dry HCl convert the aldehyde into a dimethyl acetal, protecting it, leaving the bromide intact.
3. R to S: Gabriel synthesis (phthalimide) selectively gives the primary amine. No overalkylation occurs.
4. R to T: Dry Ag₂O promotes the coupling of two alkyl halides into an ether, doubling the molecular formula. Moist Ag₂O would yield an alcohol.
design.student_must_notice: Gabriel synthesis yields exclusively a primary amine (S), giving a positive carbylamine test. Dry Ag₂O yields a symmetrical ether (T) instead of an alcohol, doubling the degree of unsaturation and number of carbons.
design.trap: Students might assume Gabriel synthesis can overalkylate to a secondary amine (failing the carbylamine test), or mistake dry Ag₂O for moist Ag₂O, yielding an alcohol (T) with half the actual degree of unsaturation.
